title: The Best ShipStation Alternative for High-Volume Shippers
summary: Looking for a ShipStation alternative? See why high-volume ecommerce and 3PL teams move to EasyPost for API-first shipping and smarter carrier selection.
body_markdown:
*Tired of working around your shipping platform? Here’s why growing ecommerce and 3PL teams move to EasyPost, and what changes when they do.*


If you’re looking for a ShipStation alternative, you probably already know why. The tool that felt easy when you were printing a few hundred labels a day has turned into something you work around. In ShipStation’s core app, carrier decisions are managed through dashboards and predefined rules, and every new carrier is one more thing to configure by hand. The bigger you get, the more shipping feels like something you manage by hand instead of something your systems just do.


EasyPost is built for the other side of that curve. It’s an API-first platform that puts shipping logic where high-volume teams actually want it: inside their own systems, running automatically. For high-volume teams that want shipping embedded in their OMS, WMS, or checkout, EasyPost is the strongest ShipStation alternative. Here’s what that looks like, and where it’s the better fit.


##


Why growing teams outgrow ShipStation


The ceiling usually isn’t a missing feature. It’s the shape of the platform.


ShipStation is organized around its dashboard, which is a good fit when a person is managing orders on a screen. It’s a different story when you’re moving thousands of labels a day and want carrier selection, label creation, and tracking to happen as part of your OMS, WMS, or checkout, without anyone clicking through an interface. At that scale, you don’t want a better screen. You want the shipping logic to run itself.


##


What you get on EasyPost


**One integration, 100+ carriers.** Connect once through a


[single shipping API](https://www.easypost.com/shipping-api) and reach USPS, UPS, FedEx, DHL, and a deep bench of regional, same-day, and cross-border carriers. Adding a carrier later doesn’t mean building a new integration.


**Carrier selection that runs itself.**[Luma AI Select](https://www.easypost.com/products/luma-ai/) rates every shipment and buys the best-value label automatically, weighing cost, delivery speed, and how carriers actually perform, then adjusting as conditions change. No analyst babysitting rules, no static strategy that slowly drifts out of date. That difference matters when the cheapest service on paper is underperforming on a lane: a configured strategy sees the quoted rate and set transit time, while Luma also sees how carriers are actually performing and adjusts before another rule goes stale.


**Rates without the negotiation.**[Wallet](https://www.easypost.com/wallet/) gives you pre-negotiated carrier rates up to 88% below retail, with no contracts to manage and no credentials to juggle.


**Reliability when volume spikes.** EasyPost maintains 99.99% uptime, helping keep label generation, rate shopping, and tracking running when volume is at its highest.


**Intelligence, not just data.**[Luma AI Insights](https://www.easypost.com/products/luma-ai/) turns your shipping data into answers, benchmarking carrier performance and modeling scenarios so you can see exactly where cost and delivery can improve.


This is what “shipping as infrastructure” looks like in practice.


[XPS Ship](https://www.easypost.com/xps-ship-case-study) , a shipping platform running on EasyPost, now moves more than a million packages a month, cut label creation from five or six seconds to 350 milliseconds, and completed its integration in two to three weeks.


##


The part most switches get wrong


Here’s what’s worth knowing before you move: changing platforms doesn’t cut costs by itself.


For teams already using several carriers, adding another creates options but doesn’t fix stale routing logic. The real leak is the shipment that still goes to the wrong carrier because the logic never caught up with current rates or performance. Letting the platform make the best-value call on every label is what closes that gap, and it’s the difference EasyPost is built around. That’s how the switch can show up in your numbers instead of only changing your workflow.


##


When ShipStation still makes sense


To be fair, ShipStation is a solid choice for teams that want an out-of-the-box interface for managing orders, printing labels, and running predefined automation without building shipping into their own stack. If that describes you, you may not need to move.


EasyPost becomes the better fit when shipping is infrastructure: when you want it running inside your systems, with more control, more scale, and carrier selection based on real performance. If you want the full feature-by-feature view, see our


[EasyPost vs. ShipStation](https://www.easypost.com/easypost-vs-shippo-vs-shipstation/) comparison.


##


What it takes to move from ShipStation to EasyPost


Moving to a single API is lighter than a typical platform migration, though it isn’t nothing. The real work is mapping what you already do: carrier accounts and service codes, special handling, labels and returns, tracking events, and the reporting that feeds the rest of your business. Once that logic is mapped, EasyPost connects your carriers, automates selection, and can run alongside your current setup until you’re ready to cut over.


The API integration is only part of the job. Deciding what your shipping logic


*should* be is the work worth doing.


##


Ready to see it on your shipments?


If ShipStation has become something you manage instead of something that works for you, EasyPost is the alternative built for where you’re headed.


[Talk to our team](https://www.easypost.com/talk-to-easypost/) and we’ll show you what changes when your platform makes the right carrier call on every label.


##


Frequently asked questions


### What is the best ShipStation alternative for high-volume shippers?


For teams shipping thousands of labels a day, EasyPost is the strongest alternative. It’s API-first, connects 100+ carriers through one integration, and automates best-value carrier selection with Luma AI so shipping runs inside your systems instead of a dashboard.


### Why do companies switch from ShipStation to EasyPost?


Companies switch when they outgrow a UI-led workflow and want shipping logic in their own systems: automated carrier selection, one integration for 100+ carriers, and reliability at scale.


### Will switching platforms lower my shipping costs?


Not on its own. Savings come from how carriers are selected on each shipment, not from the platform name. EasyPost can lower costs by automatically selecting the best-value label based on cost, speed, and actual carrier performance.


### Is EasyPost hard to integrate?


Integration time depends on your existing systems and shipping logic. XPS Ship, a shipping platform built on EasyPost, completed its integration in two to three weeks.
